name: Ahmed et al. 2018 Moisture Adsorption Isotherms of Commercial Flours
citation: Ahmed, M.W., Aziz, M.G. & Islam, M.N. (2018). Modeling of Moisture Adsorption Isotherm of Selected Commercial Flours of Bangladesh. The Agriculturists 16(2):35-42
notes: Commercial wheat atta, static gravimetric adsorption at 30 C, aw 0.11-0.93. Table 2 GAB: m0=0.0567 g/g db, C=20.82, K=0.87 (best GAB fit of 3 flours). Table 1 measured EMC (% db): aw0.52=10.67, 0.68=13.68, 0.75=15.78, 0.85=23.04. KB use: atta initial aw 0.63 (range 0.61-0.66) = aw where GAB/measured EMC equals IFCT-2017 moisture 11.10% wb (12.49% db); aw_crit 0.75 = highest measured aw whose EMC (15.78% db = 13.6% wb) stays under the FSSAI 14.0% wb atta limit (GAB gives 0.759). Note GAB under-predicts measured EMC below aw 0.5.

name: Vishwakarma et al. 2007 Sorption Isotherms of Pigeonpea Grain and Dhal
citation: Vishwakarma, R.K., Goyal, R.K. & Bhargav, V.K. (2007). Moisture Sorption Isotherms of Pigeonpea (Cajanas cajan) Grain and its Dehulled Splits (Dhal). American Journal of Food Technology 2(4):228-237
notes: Dhal (cv UPAS-120) adsorption EMC, static gravimetric, 10-50 C. Table 1 dhal at 30 C (ERH -> EMC % db): 51.4->11.89, 63.3->14.48, 71.4->17.34, 80.0->18.76, 90.7->29.17. Paper fits only modified Henderson/Chung-Pfost/Oswin/Halsey/Chen-Clayton (no GAB). KB DERIVED: GAB fitted by KB maintainers (nonlinear least squares) to the five 30 C dhal points: m0=6.89+/-0.56 % db, K=0.841+/-0.027 with C FIXED at 20 because C is not identifiable from aw>=0.51 data (free fit runs to bound); fitted EMC in aw 0.45-0.70 changes <0.6% db for C 10-500; R2=0.975. Initial aw 0.44 (0.40-0.49) = GAB aw at IFCT-2017 moisture 9.20+/-0.61% wb (extrapolated below lowest data point, lower confidence); aw_crit 0.60 = aw where EMC reaches FSSAI 12% wb limit for pulses without seed coat (13.64% db; linear interpolation of Table 1 gives 0.594, GAB fit 0.615).

name: FSSAI Food Products Standards Chapter 2.4 Cereals and Cereal Products
citation: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations 2011, Chapter 2.4 Cereals and Cereal Products, Version 4 (07.05.2025): 2.4.1(1) Wheat Flour (Atta) and 2.4.6(22) Pulses
notes: Atta moisture not more than 14.0% by mass; pulses moisture max 14%, pulses without seed coat (dal, incl. Red gram/Arhar Cajanus cajan) max 12% by mass. Used to set aw_crit via isotherm (see AHMED-2018, VISHWAKARMA-2007).

name: Doblado-Maldonado et al. 2012 Whole Wheat Flour Milling and Storage Review
citation: Doblado-Maldonado, A.F., Pike, O.A., Sweley, J.C. & Rose, D.J. (2012). Key issues and challenges in whole wheat flour milling and storage. Journal of Cereal Science 56(2):119-126
notes: Whole wheat flour shelf life shorter than white flour due to lipids and lipase/lipoxygenase; review states data insufficient for a definitive shelf life and millers' use-by dates are 3-9 months after milling (temperate-market practice, not Indian summer ambient). Used for atta storage life_days [90,270].

name: Jeelani et al. 2025 Packaging and Storage Quality of Pigeon Pea Dhal
citation: Jeelani, M., Vasudeva Rao, V., Sandeep Raja, D., Gopala Swamy, S.V.S. & Edukondalu, L. (2025). Effect of Different Packaging Materials on Storage Quality and Sensory Evaluation of Pigeon Pea Dhal. The Journal of Research ANGRAU 53(3):23-36
notes: Dhal (cv LRG 52) stored 240 d at ambient 21-37 C / 26-90% RH (Aug 2023-Mar 2024). Initial moisture 9.13% wb; final range LDPE 9.13-9.66, HDPE 9.13-9.27, BoPP 8.94-9.13, PET 8.87-9.13, jute up to 13.55% wb. Insect infestation onset: LDPE and jute 60 d, HDPE 180 d, none in BoPP/PET to 240 d. Used for toor dal life_days [60,240].
